state.persona: Matt, organizer, on his laptop where he planned the Lisbon trip. He had loved 'Walk Lisbon's best neighborhoods' and 'Cocktails in Lisbon'.
state.job: Collect friends' picks into the plan.
state.workflow_state: Opens a picks link a friend sent in the group chat. In reality the friend, when joining, tapped the 'Matt' chip instead of their own name and voted pass on both of Matt's loves.
state.visible_text: Eyebrow 'SHARED TRIP'. Headline 'Matt sent their picks. 2 votes.' Lede 'Add them to your trip. If they voted before, their new picks replace the old ones.' Single button [Add their picks]. After tapping: 'Matt's 2 picks are in.' and [See the group's faves →]. No preview of which picks, no sender device info, no warning that the name matches the organizer, no undo.
state.result: Matt's own two loves are replaced by two passes on his device.

notices_problem.instructions: Probability Matt notices before tapping 'Add their picks' that something is wrong (a picks link claiming to be from himself).

would_tap_add.instructions: Probability Matt taps 'Add their picks' anyway.

can_recover.instructions: Probability Matt later realizes his own loves were overwritten and restores them correctly.

stale_order.instructions: Separate scenario: Priya sent two picks links (first loved the Rooftop, later changed her mind and passed). Matt opens the newer one, then later taps the older one in the chat; the page says 'Priya sent their picks. 1 votes. Add them to your trip. If they voted before, their new picks replace the old ones.' Probability Matt realizes the older link will overwrite Priya's newer choice.
